title: Sid Catlett dies in her arms at a JATP concert
summary: Backstage at a Jazz at the Philharmonic show, Sid Catlett was holding her, then collapsed and died as she walked away. The stage manager put her on stage next because he feared she would panic.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Another very nice drummer was Sid Catlett.
Oh, yess indeed. He was really one of the greatest. I told you he almost died holding me.

I was at the Jazz Philharmic and we did a thing and he came down to see us. He was working there. And he was standing back stage, you know, and he was standing there with his arms around me, just standing there talking just watching the show and then I said, 'well Sid I got to go and check on my make-up and get ready because I go on next'. And he said, 'okay'. And I walked away and as I walked away from him I heard something go 'plop' and I looked around and he was stretched out on the floor.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

So the stage man came and he said, "Helen you go on right after this". I said, "okay". And they put me on because they thought Sid and I were something, I guess. And that's what happened. He never did come to, he died.
That was the end of it?
Oh my goodness. Helen, I didn't know. I thought he'd had an attack before that or something. I didn't know. Well you know if you have to go, that is a great way to go, I would think. Wouldn't you?
I mean, no warning. That wouldn't be too bad, and with your arms around Helen Humes? Oh, it must have been terrible for you.
Yeah. Even when I got through singing I went back there and they had him all covered up.
Oh my goodness, what an awful thing. I didn't know that. Did you close? Was that the end?
No. He put me on because he said I might panic.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
